QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_40

question.text: Equity capital is also called 'risk capital' because:

answer.text: Equity investors accept the risk that the business may succeed or fail without expecting a fixed rate of regular return
Equity investors receive guaranteed returns regardless of business performance
Equity shares can only be bought during high-risk market conditions
The government guarantees all equity investments against losses

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity capital is called risk capital because equity investors are willing to take the risk that the business may succeed or fail without expecting a fixed rate of regular return. They invest with a view to participate in the success of the business, which would translate into a higher value of their investment. The Trap: Equity does not provide guaranteed returns (option B). Equity can be purchased in any market condition (option C). No government guarantee exists for equity investments (option D). Note: The defining trait of risk capital is the absence of a contractual fixed return — the upside and downside both flow from business performance.
